overview: The sign-update packet is a thin but real anticheat surface. NoCheatPlus runs its AutoSign blockplace check on sign edits, timing the edit against the placement and the line content, and Intave kicks players whose sign lines exceed a length limit, which is the crash-exploit angle of this packet.

checks.name: AutoSign (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Catch instant sign-text macros that fill all four lines faster than a human can type.
checks.how_it_works: After a sign is placed, the blockplace listener stores a block hash and the open time. On the sign edit, the check compares the block hash, then estimates the minimum human edit time from the line count and the distinct characters (150 ms base, 50 ms per extra line, 50 ms per character). An edit faster than the estimate flags, with the violation level scaled by the time deficit.
checks.detects: Auto-sign macros, instant sign spam, and sign edits sent against a different block than the one placed.
checks.variations: Intave's ItemCrashTracker instead validates sign content length (see next entry); Vrekt-Arc-v2 and Artemis only ship UpdateSign wrappers.

checks.name: ItemCrashTracker sign limit (Intave)
checks.purpose: Block the sign-update crash exploit that sends oversized line components.
checks.how_it_works: Subscribes to the UPDATE_SIGN packet, reads the four chat components, and if any JSON serialization exceeds 500 characters it cancels the packet and kicks the player. The same module also carries Intave's window-click crash fix.
checks.detects: Sign update packets with oversized or malformed line components, which crash vanilla sign handling on 1.8 servers.
checks.variations: No other anticheat in the corpus validates sign content; the rest ignore the packet entirely.
